text: "I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge." Hebrews puts those words in Jesus' mouth. He deserved every promise of Psalm 91, and gave up its protection on the cross so you could have it.
explanation:
Hebrews quotes Jesus saying, "I will put My trust in Him." As a man, He trusted and obeyed His Father perfectly, so if anyone merited Psalm 91, He did. Yet the One promised long life died at thirty-three, forsaken, with no protection.

He took your place so that you could take His. Every promise in this psalm is yours by grace, paid for with His blood. And when He says, "Because you have made the Lord, who is my refuge… your dwelling place, no evil shall befall you," that's Jesus speaking to you. Don't let anyone explain "no evil" away as flowery language. God means what He says.

text: The devil quoted Psalm 91 to Jesus but stopped before "you shall tread upon the lion and the cobra." He couldn't quote his own defeat.
explanation:
On the pinnacle of the temple, Satan urged Jesus to jump, "for it is written, He shall give His angels charge over you." It's the only time the devil quotes Scripture, and he quoted it wrongly. The promise isn't about stunts. It's about walking through life with angels lifting you over traps you can't even see.

Why that psalm? Perhaps because believers have thrown it at him for centuries. Notice what he left out: "The young lion and the serpent you shall trample underfoot." Whether the enemy comes roaring openly or slithering in secret, he's under your feet. When you speak to him, point down.

text: Angels heed "the voice of His word." The Bible on your shelf has no voice until you give it one.
explanation:
"Bless the Lord, you His angels, who excel in strength, who do His word, heeding the voice of His word." When the angel came to Daniel, he said, "I have come because of your words." Angels aren't chubby cherubs with harps; they're mighty. And they are "ministering spirits sent forth to minister for" (not merely to) the heirs of salvation: they wait for your instruction.

Jesus said He could summon twelve legions of angels: more than seventy thousand. So speak His Word over your day: "Father, thank You, no evil shall befall me, and no plague shall come near my dwelling." When you give voice to God's Word, His angels respond.

text: His car flew off a hill road. The women in the back shouted "Jesus!" The car stopped in mid-air and came down like it was landing on feathers.
explanation:
Joseph Prince's uncle, then far from God, was driving some elderly prayer warriors to a wedding in Malaysia when his car skidded off a sharp bend on a hillside. Mid-air, the women cried out the name of Jesus. The car seemed to halt, then dropped straight down and landed softly. The next week he was back in church, and he has kept coming.

When there's no time for a long prayer, His name is enough. "I will set him on high, because he has known My name." God "has given Him the name which is above every name": above cancer, accident and death. At the name of Jesus every knee must bow.

text: The Bible never says you have an appointed time to die. It says, "It is appointed for men to die once." And some things lengthen your days.
explanation:
"When it's your time, it's your time" isn't Scripture. Hebrews says it's appointed for men to die once, not at a fixed hour. Lazarus died twice, and the generation alive at the rapture won't die at all. Fate isn't in the Bible. Faith is.

Scripture does say some choices prolong life and some shorten it. "The fear of the Lord prolongs days": worshipping Him adds to your life. Honouring your parents brings long life; a lying tongue "is but for a moment." Living in sin with no desire to change drains life away. That's why John says, "If anyone sees his brother sinning… he will ask, and He will give him life."

text: "As your God, I judge the world. As your Father, I judge no one."
explanation:
Jesus said, "The Father judges no one." God will judge the nations, but to His children He is Father, and the Father isn't sitting in judgment over you. There's a revival of interest in the Hebrew names of God, and they're precious. But the name above them, the one Jesus came to reveal, is "Father": Abba, Daddy.

Listen to how you pray. "O God… O God" can carry a sense of distance; anyone can say "God." "Father" speaks of nearness. Psalm 91 ends with two conditions: "Because he has set his love upon Me" and "because he has known My name." Know Him as Father, and love His Son.

text: Three of David's men broke through enemy lines just to bring him a drink from Bethlehem's well. God recorded their names. Joab, his army commander, isn't on the list.
explanation:
Hiding in the cave of Adullam, David sighed, "Oh, that someone would give me a drink of the water from the well of Bethlehem!" Three mighty men risked their lives through a Philistine garrison simply because they loved him. Their deed is written in Scripture's list of David's mighty men, while Joab, who fought many battles for his own advancement, is missing.

A woman broke an alabaster flask worth a year's wages over Jesus' head. The disciples called it waste. Jesus said that wherever the gospel is preached, what she did will be told as a memorial to her. Big or small doesn't matter. What's done out of love for Jesus is what lasts.
